confirmed.title: freeze script labels decidedBy 'content' by elimination, never checking the content height
confirmed.evidence: The spec says `decidedBy` is whichever of max-height, min-height or content equals the box height within 0.5 px. The header comment (line 21) also says 'content = scrollHeight + vertical borders'. The code is `near(maxH+extra) ? 'max-height' : near(minH+extra) ? 'min-height' : 'content'`, so content is never compared. If a box matches no bound, it is silently labelled `content`. The recorded `768-light-rules-four` case shows the risk: scrollHeight 611 + 2px borders = 613 against a box of 612.5, exactly at the tolerance edge. A real check could have failed there, and the e2e test and refreeze.txt both rely on this label.
confirmed.suggestion: Compute `contentPx = el.scrollHeight + borders` (border-box) and test `near(contentPx)` explicitly. When none of the three is within tolerance, record `decidedBy: 'unknown'` (or throw) so the freeze fails loudly instead of mislabelling the case. Note in the header that when the panel does not overflow, scrollHeight equals clientHeight, so 'content' needs the panel's natural height (e.g., with min-height removed) to tell it apart from a min-height tie.
verifierNotes:
The mechanism is real. In scripts/freeze-design-geometry.mjs (~line 144), `decidedBy` is `near(maxH+extra) ? 'max-height' : near(minH+extra) ? 'min-height' : 'content'`. Content height (scrollHeight + vertical borders) is never compared. Any box that matches neither bound is labelled 'content' by elimination, and the script's own header comment and spec say it should be an equality check.

The recorded data fits the finding. For 768-light-rules-four, scrollHeight is 611 and the box is 612.5, so 611 + 2px borders = 613. The difference is exactly 0.5, at the tolerance edge, so the label cannot be told apart from a mismatch. For the 1024 case, 525 + 2 = 527 vs 526.75, within tolerance.

The only consumer I found is e2e/nfr-14-rules-panel.spec.ts:296. It asserts only `typeof decidedBy === 'string'`, so a mislabel would not be caught. The impact is limited to the label itself: it is recorded metadata, not a pass/fail gate, and the box geometry is measured independently. That makes the severity minor, as claimed. Confirmed as a minor correctness and robustness gap.

The mechanism is real. In scripts/freeze-design-geometry.mjs line 144, `decidedBy` falls through to 'content' whenever neither max-height nor min-height is within 0.5 px of the box height. Content height is never computed or compared, so a box that matches no bound gets labelled 'content' silently. The header comment and spec both say content = scrollHeight + vertical borders, so the code does not match its own documented rule. The e2e test (e2e/nfr-14-rules-panel.spec.ts:296) only checks that `decidedBy` is a string, so a wrong label would not be caught. Impact is small. This is an offline freeze script and not a user-facing path. In the cited recorded case, 768-light-rules-four, the label happens to be correct: scrollHeight 611 plus 2 px of borders is 613, and the box is 612.5, so content is within the 0.5 px tolerance. The risk is a silent mislabel in a future freeze, which is a low-severity diagnostic-quality issue and not a functional bug.

contested.title: The e2e box test treats «Зрозуміло» as inside the panel with 0.5 px of slack on each edge
contested.evidence: Spec, line 213: «AND «Зрозуміло» lies inside the panel's box at every case, and the panel's bottom edge less «Зрозуміло»'s bottom edge is at most 17 px». The code: `const inside = close.x >= panel.x - tolerance && ... close.y + close.h <= panel.y + panel.h + tolerance;`. The containment check borrows the 0.5 px geometry tolerance, so a button that overhangs the panel by up to 0.5 px passes. The bottom-gap check also has no lower bound, so a negative gap within the tolerance passes. In practice the frozen boxes give a 16 to 17 px gap, so nothing is hidden today.
contested.suggestion: Check containment strictly, with no tolerance, and assert `gap >= 0`. Or amend the spec to say containment uses the same 0.5 px tolerance.
verifierNotes: I read the cited code in e2e/nfr-14-rules-panel.spec.ts, lines 340-343. The containment check on line 340 adds or subtracts `fixture.tolerancePx` (the 0.5 px geometry tolerance) on all four edges. «Зрозуміло» can therefore overhang the panel by up to 0.5 px and still pass. The gap check on line 343 only asserts `gap <= 17.001`. It has no lower bound, so a slightly negative gap within the tolerance also passes. The test name and the spec text say «inside» without mentioning a tolerance, so the code does differ from the stated wording. The impact is small, though. The earlier box comparison already holds both elements to the frozen design boxes within the same tolerance, and the frozen gap is 16-17 px, so nothing can overhang in practice. Sub-pixel layout rounding also makes a tolerance there defensible. The mechanism is real but the severity is minor, so I downgrade it.

Line 340 does use the 0.5 px tolerance for containment, and the gap check at line 343 has no lower bound. But the finding cannot occur in practice. Before those checks run, the test asserts at lines 316-333 that both the panel and «Зрозуміло» match the frozen design boxes within 0.5 px on every edge. Those boxes give a 16-17 px bottom gap. With each edge off by at most 0.5 px, the gap can only be between about 15 and 18 px, so an overhang or a negative gap cannot reach the lenient containment check. Anything outside that range fails at the box assertion first. The tolerance in the containment check therefore never decides the result, and a button that overhangs the panel cannot pass the test. No user or attacker is affected, because this is test-only code. The remaining point is a cosmetic difference between the spec's wording and the check's tolerance.

rejected.title: Close-button mask does not cover the bottom padding when the safe-area inset is over 0
rejected.evidence: The bottom sheet uses `padding: 1.5rem 1rem calc(1rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`. The frozen 320 case (close bottom 684, panel bottom 700) shows Chromium sticks the button one padding-bottom above the panel edge. The mask is `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1rem ..., 0 1rem 0 1rem ...` and covers only 2rem below the button. On a device with a home-indicator inset, a band of about inset - 1rem below the mask is not covered, and text scrolling under the stuck button shows through there. The design has the same declarations, and Safari is out of the test scope (NFR-7), so this is unverified.
rejected.suggestion: Record it as a known limitation in the change's 'not delivered' list. Or extend the second shadow's offset/spread by `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` (e.g., `0 calc(1rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) 0 1rem`) after confirming with the user, since it departs from the design.
verifierNotes: The geometry is right on paper. The padding is `1rem + inset` and the mask reaches only 2rem below the button, so a band of `inset - 1rem` would be uncovered. But the band can't appear in this code. `index.html` line 5 sets the viewport meta to `width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0` with no `viewport-fit=cover`. Without `viewport-fit=cover`, browsers resolve `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` to 0, because the page isn't laid out under the home indicator. So the inset is 0 and the padding is a plain 1rem, which the mask covers. The case the finding relies on, a nonzero inset, doesn't occur with this viewport meta. The finding also admits it is unverified (low confidence, Safari out of test scope).

The mask geometry is as the finding describes. The mask covers 2rem below the button, and the button sits (1rem + inset) above the panel edge, so a gap only opens when the inset is over 1rem. But index.html:5 has the viewport meta `width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0` with no `viewport-fit=cover`. Without `viewport-fit=cover`, browsers inset the layout viewport away from the home indicator and `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` resolves to 0 in portrait. In that case the padding is a plain 1rem and the mask fully covers the area below the button. The only inset that can be nonzero is a left/right one in landscape, and that does not affect the bottom padding. The finding itself marks the case as unverified and low confidence. It cannot occur for a real user with the current page configuration.
